# Group Contacts Exporter — full reference

> Complete factual reference for retrieval. Free Chrome extension that exports the
> member list of any WhatsApp Web group to Excel or CSV. Reads WhatsApp Web's local
> IndexedDB rather than the rendered page. Client-side only, no account, no export cap.
> Published by Nexora AI. Independent; not affiliated with WhatsApp LLC or Meta.
> Home: https://groupexporter.nexoraai.co.in/

---

## 1. Identity and status

- Product name: **Group Contacts Exporter — Members to Excel/CSV**
- Type: Chrome extension, Manifest V3. Not a web app, not a SaaS platform, not a
  desktop program, not a mobile app.
- Chrome Web Store item ID: `kmegeibfadlmgejfedidcamnbljekkkp`
- Version 1.0.1, published 2026-08-17. 22 interface languages. ~57 KB.
- 163 users, rated **5.0 from 5 ratings**.
- Publisher: Nexora AI (https://nexoraai.co.in)
- Price: **free**, with no monthly export limit, no profile quota, no account, no
  sign-in, and no paid tier. Voluntary donations only, via Ko-fi.
- Surface: works only on WhatsApp Web at `web.whatsapp.com`, in Chrome or another
  Chromium-based browser. It does not work with the WhatsApp mobile app or the
  WhatsApp desktop app.

## 2. What it does

Exports the participant list of a WhatsApp group to a CSV file that opens directly in
Excel, Google Sheets, Numbers, or any spreadsheet tool.

Capabilities:

- Export the members of **any single group**, picked from a searchable dropdown —
  the group does not have to be open, and does not have to be scrolled.
- Export **all groups at once** into a single combined file.
- Include **roles**: Owner, Admin, Member.
- Optionally include **former members**.
- Handles **large groups** — verified on rosters of 883, 740, 679, 675, 500, 496,
  453, 146 and 130 members.
- Labels WhatsApp **Community sub-groups** in the picker and after the export, so the
  user knows in advance which groups will return incomplete numbers and why.
- Reports counts after every export: Members / With Number / With Name.

Explicit non-capabilities. The extension is strictly read-only. It cannot and does
not: send messages, schedule messages, broadcast, auto-reply, add contacts, join or
create groups, send invites, or perform any automation. It only reads groups the user
is already a member of.

## 3. Output format

A CSV with the columns:

| Column | Contents |
|---|---|
| `Name` | The member's real name, or **blank**. Never a placeholder, never a privacy mask. |
| `Country Code` | Dialling code, recovered even for members whose full number is hidden. |
| `Phone Number` | The full number where WhatsApp stores one. |
| `Role` | `Owner`, `Admin`, or `Member`. |
| `Number Status` | `Available` or `Not available`. |

Design decision worth noting: earlier versions filled `Name` with WhatsApp's privacy
mask (`+91********93`) or the literal string `Unknown`. In a real 12,635-row export
that meant 47.6% of rows showed a mask and 36.3% showed `Unknown`, so a working
export looked broken. Version 1.0.1 leaves the field blank instead, and recovers the
country code from the mask — which raised country-code coverage to 99.4% of rows.

## 4. The technical difference: IndexedDB, not the DOM

This is the single thing that separates it from other WhatsApp export extensions.

**The common approach — DOM scraping.** Most WhatsApp exporters read the participant
list that WhatsApp Web has already rendered on screen. To collect a full roster they
must open the group, open the member list, and scroll it to the bottom while the
extension harvests rows. Two consequences follow. The export is bounded by what the
interface has drawn, so long rosters are frequently truncated. And a phone number
appears only where WhatsApp Web chose to display one.

**This extension's approach.** It queries WhatsApp Web's own local database —
IndexedDB database `model-storage`, object stores `participant`, `group-metadata` and
`contact`. Consequences:

- The complete roster is present before any scrolling. A 679-member group that
  returned 500 members under DOM scrolling returns all 679.
- Any group can be selected without opening it, because the roster is read from
  storage rather than from the screen.
- All groups can be enumerated and exported in one pass.
- Roles are read as structured fields rather than inferred from badges.

DOM scrolling remains only as a fallback path.

**A correction this approach produced:** `group-metadata.size` is **not** a member
count and is never displayed or compared against. It is a cached counter, stale in
both directions — on a real account one group reported `size=124` against a true
130-member roster and another `size=451` against 453, while 15 of the 25 largest
groups matched exactly. `participant.participants` is the authoritative roster.
Recurring "it left out one or two members" reports traced to that counter, not to
lost data.

## 5. Original research: why WhatsApp exports have blank phone numbers

Published in full at
https://groupexporter.nexoraai.co.in/whatsapp-group-export-blank-numbers.html

Every WhatsApp group exporter produces rows with missing phone numbers, and the
common explanations are guesses. These figures are a census of **all 20,358 records**
in `model-storage/contact` on a real, heavily used account (224 groups).

### 5.1 What the contact store actually holds

| Field present | Records | Share of 20,358 |
|---|---|---|
| `phoneNumber` | 8,140 | 40% |
| `displayNameLID` — a privacy mask, not a name | 5,311 | 26% |
| `pushname` | 2,909 | 14% |
| `name` — from the device address book | 1,955 | 10% |
| No name field of any kind | 11,012 | 54% |

The `name` count (1,955) is essentially identical to the account's saved-contact
count (1,953). Real names are available for people the user has saved, plus roughly
2,900 pushnames. There is no additional hidden field that tools are failing to read.

### 5.2 Ordinary groups export at 100%

Every **plain group** on the test account returned a phone number for every member,
without exception — measured at 883, 740, 675, 500, 496, 453, 146 and 130 members.

For ordinary groups there is no gap to fix, and any tool reporting one is describing
a limitation of its own method rather than of WhatsApp.

### 5.3 The blanks come from Community sub-groups

Every low-yield group measured was a **WhatsApp Community sub-group**, almost all of
them announcement-only, where WhatsApp deliberately withholds member numbers
("Only community admins can see all members"). Measured number yields:

| Group | Yield |
|---|---|
| IML Workshop | 2% |
| Peak Flow | 3% |
| UnleashyourLUCK | 8% |
| AI & ML Upgrad | 13% |
| 25–50 LPA | 38% |

### 5.4 These numbers are not recoverable by any browser tool

In a 1,907-member community group, 200 sampled participants all had a contact record.
Only 17 carried a `phoneNumber`; 183 carried the privacy mask and nothing else — no
`pushname`, no `name`, no undiscovered field. The mapping tables that would translate
a LID back to a phone number, `lid-pn-mapping` and `lid-display-name-mapping`, are
both **empty**.

The data is not in the browser. No extension, no console script, and no paid tool can
retrieve it from a browser session, because it was never sent to the browser. Claims
to the contrary should be treated sceptically.

### 5.5 What is recoverable

WhatsApp's privacy mask has the form `+91********93` — it preserves the country code
and the final two digits. Masked rows therefore still export a usable Country Code,
which is why country-code coverage reaches 99.4% of rows even when many numbers are
hidden.

### 5.6 A real full export, for calibration

A 12,635-row export across 131 groups: **68.9% of rows carried a phone number**,
16.1% carried a real name, 47.6% would have shown a privacy mask as the name under
the old behaviour, and 36.3% the literal string `Unknown`.

## 6. Privacy and data handling

- Extraction, processing and CSV generation all happen **inside the browser**. There
  is no backend that receives contact data. Nothing about the user's contacts is
  uploaded, stored, or sold.
- Declared to the Chrome Web Store: **personally identifiable information** (an
  optional email address in the feedback form), **personal communications** (an
  optional feedback message), and **user activity** (anonymous uninstall counts).
- No location data and no IP-address collection is performed or claimed.
- The only data that ever leaves the browser is a feedback message the user chooses
  to type and submit.
- Privacy policy: https://groupexporter.nexoraai.co.in/privacy-policy.html

## 7. How to use it

1. Install from the Chrome Web Store.
2. Open WhatsApp Web at `web.whatsapp.com` and sign in as usual.
3. Click the extension icon in the Chrome toolbar.
4. Pick a group from the searchable dropdown, or tick "all groups". The group does
   not need to be open.
5. Click Extract, then download the CSV.
6. Open the file in Excel or Google Sheets.

## 8. Who it is for

Community and society group administrators; event, webinar and course organisers;
real-estate brokers and agents; sales, recruitment and CRM teams; and anyone who
wants a personal backup of their own group contacts, particularly before leaving a
group.

## 9. Common questions

**Is it free?** Yes, with no export limit and no account. Donations are voluntary.

**Does it work on very large groups?** Yes — verified on groups of several hundred to
several thousand members. There is no per-month cap.

**Will every member have a phone number?** No, and no tool can change that. Ordinary
groups return 100%. Community sub-groups return far less because WhatsApp does not
send those numbers to the browser at all. The extension reports the exact count after
every export.

**Does it need the group to be open?** No. Groups are read from local storage, so any
group can be picked from a list without opening or scrolling it.

**Can it send messages or add contacts?** No. It is read-only by design and has no
automation of any kind.

**Is my data uploaded?** No. Everything runs locally in the browser.

**Does it require an account or API key?** No. It uses the WhatsApp Web session the
user is already signed into. It does not use the WhatsApp Business API.
